label: Digitally Immersed & Emotionally Distressed
summary: This profile represents highly educated women who spend more than 5 hours daily online and report elevated levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety. With a UCLA-8 loneliness mean of 1.74, PHQ-9 depression mean of 1.75, and notably high GAD-7 anxiety mean of 2.17, this group consistently scores above average on all three distress indicators. The combination of extensive screen time and graduate-level education suggests individuals who may be heavily engaged in digital work or social environments yet experience significant emotional isolation and psychological burden.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate-level education or above, daily screen time exceeding 5 hours
behavior_markers: Elevated loneliness despite likely high digital connectivity
Highest anxiety levels among profiles (GAD-7 mean 2.17)
Extended daily screen time of more than 5 hours
Potential reliance on digital environments for social or professional engagement
tone: Anxious, emotionally burdened, and socially disconnected despite high digital engagement

label: Well-Adjusted Male Graduate
summary: This profile represents respondents who report notably low levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms. With UCLA-8 loneliness scores, PHQ-9 depression scores, and GAD-7 anxiety scores all well below typical midpoints, these individuals appear to be psychologically well-adjusted and emotionally stable. They spend a moderate amount of time (1–3 hours) on activities captured by the study, suggesting balanced engagement rather than excessive or minimal use.
demographic_anchor: Male, graduate-level education or above, 1–3 hours of daily usage
behavior_markers: Very low loneliness scores (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 0.77), indicating strong social connectedness
Minimal depressive symptoms (PHQ-9 mean ≈ 0.33), suggesting positive mood and functional well-being
Near-floor anxiety levels (GAD-7 mean ≈ 0.09), reflecting emotional calm and low worry
Moderate daily usage of 1–3 hours, consistent with balanced and non-compulsive engagement
Highly educated background, potentially associated with greater coping resources

label: Lonely but Emotionally Resilient
summary: This profile captures respondents who report notably elevated loneliness yet maintain relatively low levels of depressive and anxiety symptoms. Despite feeling socially disconnected, they do not exhibit the affective distress typically associated with loneliness, suggesting a degree of emotional resilience or effective coping that buffers against mood and anxiety disorders.
demographic_anchor: Predominantly female, holding graduate-level education or above, with moderate daily screen/internet use of 1–3 hours
behavior_markers: Reports higher-than-average loneliness (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 1.30) indicating frequent feelings of social isolation
Maintains low depressive symptomatology (PHQ-9 mean ≈ 0.86), well below clinical thresholds
Exhibits low anxiety symptoms (GAD-7 mean ≈ 0.91), suggesting minimal worry or nervousness
Moderate internet/screen engagement (1–3 hours daily), neither highly connected nor disconnected digitally
Loneliness appears decoupled from mood disturbance, suggesting possible compensatory coping strategies
tone: Quietly isolated yet psychologically stable; socially under-connected but not emotionally overwhelmed
